newsitem.title: UK: Boots launches nationwide loyalty card.
newsitem.headline: Boots launches nationwide loyalty card.

text.p: Pharmacist and retailer Boots CO Plc on Wednesday announced the nationwide launch of its Advantage customer loyalty card from September 1.
The company said total investment in the loyalty programme would be 52 million pounds up to 2000, with 25 million in 1997/98, 14 million in 1998/99 and 13 million in 1999/2000.
The retailer, Britain's biggest pharmacy group, said it expected around a four percent increase in sales from the card by the end of 1998/99, making it self-funding by the end of that year.

Customers signing up for the card will receive one point worth one pence, for every 25 pence spent in Boots The Chemists. The points can be redeemed against a range of 10,000 health and beauty products and services sold by the company.
The firm's decision to start a loyalty scheme follows moves by three of Britain's big four food superstores, including Tesco Plc and J. Sainsbury Plc, to introduce loyalty cards.
Based on two regional trials running since October 1995, Boots expects to have more than eight million of its customers holding cards by September 1998.

The card will carry a computer chip, which will give Boots the capacity to develop a high-quality information database on shopping patterns. Boots said this was more powerful than traditional market research or existing point of sale systems data.
Boots the Chemist managing director Steve Russell said in a statement: "We believe that the Advantage Card will become Britain's largest loyalty scheme."
